title: Evaluation Provenance Ledger and Mixed-Precision Rollout Manifest
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Defines a canonical provenance ledger format for evaluation artifacts and prescribes a guarded rollout checklist for mixed-precision (quantized) deployments. The goal is reproducible artifact lineage, rapid triage of regressions introduced by precision changes, and clear telemetry to drive safe rollouts.
body:
Overview
This document defines the evaluation provenance ledger (EPL) schema, storage conventions, and an operational manifest for rolling mixed-precision model variants (e.g., FP16 -> INT8 or hybrid quant) through our eval and shadow environments before production promotion. It bridges eval-harness outputs, model-onboarding checkpoints, and runtime telemetry used by regression triage.

Scope
- Applies to all evaluations and probes used for model promotion, shadow validation, and regression bisecting for mixed-precision and quant-migration efforts.
- Covers: provenance records produced by the eval-harness, artifact storage paths, hash and signing conventions, telemetry fields required by triage runbooks, and the staged rollout checklist.
- Excludes: training data lineage (handled by Data Platform) and customer PII transformation rules (see privacy sandbox docs).

Why a ledger matters
- Reproducibility: Every eval artifact must map to an immutable record so a failing probe can be replayed against the exact artifact and runtime.
- Triage speed: Standardized fields let the regression-hunting automation correlate anomalies to runtime/kernel/quant changes.
- Auditing: Rollout manifest provides a compact audit trail for mixed-precision migrations required by compliance.

EPL (Evaluation Provenance Ledger) record format
- Each evaluation run MUST emit an EPL record and push it to the artifacts index. The record is a small YAML/JSON metadata file stored next to artifacts. Example (YAML):

  eval_id: "epl-2026-000124"
  timestamp: "2026-02-09T21:16:03Z"
  probe_set_id: "priming-cohort-v3"
  model_suite: "redwood-small-7b"
  model_commit: "6a3b9c2"
  model_build_tag: "redwood-small-7b:2026-02-01"
  quant_profile_version: "qpv-2026-01-15-int8-hedge-v2"
  runtime_fingerprint: "runt-fw-1.8.2+kernels-2026-01-20"
  runtime_bin_sha: "sha256:4f9a8e..."
  seed_and_rng: "seed=20260209-42"
  dataset_hashes:
    - "prompts:sha256:ab12..."
    - "labels:sha256:9f3d..."
  batch_profile: "microburst-16-lowlatency"
  kv_cache_config: "enabled,cache_ttl=30m"
  host_gpu_arch: "nvidia-h100-80gb"
  docker_image: "redwood/eval-runner:v1.27"
  artifacts_url: "s3://eval-artifacts/epl-2026-000124/"
  metrics_summary:
    - "embedding_stability:0.012"
    - "coherence_delta:-0.03"
    - "latency_p95_ms:128"
    - "token_cost_delta_per_1k:0.74"
  signature: "sig:v1:base64..."

Notes on the record format and constraints:
- All hashes use sha256 and are hex-prefixed.
- quant_profile_version must reference a formal quant profile artifact from the quant registry.
- runtime_fingerprint encodes serving runtime major/minor, kernel set date, and any experimental flags.
- signature is an HMAC-SHA256 over the canonicalized YAML; signing key is the eval-harness service key (rotated quarterly).

Storage and naming conventions
- Artifact path template: s3://eval-artifacts/{year}/{model_suite}/{eval_id}/
- EPL metadata is saved as metadata.yaml next to artifacts and copied into the artifacts index database.
- Retention: metadata kept indefinitely; large artifacts kept for 90 days by default, with TTL extensions for promoted runs.

Searchable index fields (required)
- eval_id, model_suite, model_commit, quant_profile_version, probe_set_id, timestamp, host_gpu_arch, runtime_bin_sha, artifacts_url.
- Index entries MUST include a small metrics vector (embedding_stability, coherence_delta, latency_p95_ms) for fast queries.

Rollout manifest: staged promotion for mixed-precision variants
Purpose: Reduce blast radius when deploying quantized variants and ensure each stage is reversible with traceable provenance.

Rollout stages (numbered checklist)
1) Local dev & micro-evals
   - Owner: model-onboarding team
   - Run: full EPL metadata produced for the quant profile against a mini-probe set (N=500).
   - Acceptance: no coherence_delta worse than -0.05; embedding_stability <= 0.02.
2) Shadow (isolated shadow mesh)
   - Owner: eval-harness + serving-runtime
   - Run: shadow traffic replay for 48 hours with replica ratio 1:1000; collect EPL and streaming telemetry.
   - Acceptance: pass functional sentinels (safety/hedge tests), latency_p95 within 1.25x baseline, no token_cost_delta > +1.5x.
3) Canary (tenant-limited rolling canary)
   - Owner: platform ops
   - Run: 48–72 hours, ramp to 3% traffic segmented by low-risk tenants; EPL records must link to each canary snapshot.
   - Acceptance: per-tenant quality thresholds: NPS-equivalent probe acceptance rate >= 98%, embedding drift < 0.03, no SEV on functioncall stability.
4) Multi-tenant confidence window
   - Owner: product + platform
   - Run: 7 days at 10–20% traffic; additional human-in-the-loop review for flagged probes.
   - Acceptance: no priority regressions, ops runbook readiness validated.
5) Full promotion
   - Owner: release lead
   - Run: promote artifact tag to catalog and mark EPL provenance as promoted (promoted=true). Update retention policy to 1 year.

Rollback triggers (automated)
- Any SEV-level alert mapped to the promoted artifact_runtime_bin_sha within the last 2 hours.
- embedding_stability delta > 0.05 vs baseline for 5-minute rolling window.
- sustained latency_p95 > 2x baseline for > 10 minutes.

Rollback procedure (numbered)
1) Mark artifact as blocked in the model catalog and set promoted=false.
2) Trigger automated routing policy: shift traffic to the last known good commit according to EPL history.
3) Notify stakeholders: #ops-oncall, model-owner, product. Include eval_id and artifacts_url in message.
4) Open regression investigation ticket and attach EPL metadata, telemetry snapshot, and failing probe list.

Triaging with the EPL: a step-by-step example
1) Detection: alert for rise in functioncall failure rate. Alert payload includes runtime_bin_sha and recent eval_ids.
2) Correlate: query the artifacts index for eval runs with matching runtime_bin_sha and quant_profile_version within the last 7 days.
3) Reproduce: fetch metadata.yaml and artifacts_url for the top candidate eval_id, reproduce the run locally using docker_image and seed_and_rng.
4) Isolate: run the same probe set under FP16 and the candidate quant profile; collect metric diffs.
5) Hypothesis: if failure maps to a kernel mismatch, escalate to kernel team; if mapping to quant_profile_version, use quant rollback checklist.

Telemetry fields required by regression automation
- eval_id (string)
- runtime_bin_sha (string)
- quant_profile_version (string)
- host_gpu_arch (string)
- probe_set_id (string)
- embedding_stability (float)
- coherence_delta (float)
- functioncall_error_rate (float)
- latency_p95_ms (float)
- token_cost_delta_per_1k (float)

Operational playbook snippets
- Quick repro CLI (example):
  docker run --rm -v /tmp/artifacts:/artifacts redwood/eval-runner:v1.27 \
    --eval-id epl-2026-000124 --probes /artifacts/prompts.json --model-tag redwood-small-7b:2026-02-01 \
    --quant-profile qpv-2026-01-15-int8-hedge-v2 --seed 20260209-42 --out /artifacts/replay_result.json

- Checking a provenance record: (jq-friendly example)
  aws s3 cp s3://eval-artifacts/2026/redwood-small-7b/epl-2026-000124/metadata.yaml - | yq e . - && jq .metrics_summary replay_result.json

Security and signing
- All EPL records for canary or promoted runs MUST be signed by the eval-runner service using the eval-harness key.
- Access to artifact buckets requires role-based ACLs: read for platform and model-onboarding; write only by eval-harness service principal.

Governance and review cadence
- Every quarter, the model-onboarding and quant teams run a review of promoted EPL records and collect lessons into a quarterly migration report.
- Any promoted quant profile with two or more production incidents in a quarter must be paused and triaged under the cross-team incident process.

Appendix: Example queries and dashboards
- Minimal dashboard panels to create in Grafana:
  - "EPL Promotions": count of promoted=true by week, filterable by model_suite and quant_profile_version.
  - "Embedding Stability Heatmap": avg embedding_stability by probe_set_id and quant_profile_version.
  - "Runtime Fingerprint Error Correlation": time-series of functioncall_error_rate annotated with runtime_bin_sha changes.

- Helpful index queries (Elasticsearch-style):
  POST /epl-index/_search
  {"query": {"bool": {"must": [{"term": {"runtime_bin_sha": "sha256:4f9a8e..."}}, {"range": {"timestamp": {"gte": "now-7d/d"}}}]}}}

If you are implementing EPL emission in a new eval runner, open a PR that includes: schema validation tests, signing integration, and at least one sample metadata.yaml for a real probe run.
